step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes a near real-time anomaly detection system for S3 access logs. Client S3 buckets (Client 1, Client 2, Client N) generate access logs, which are delivered to a dedicated S3 Access Logs bucket. This log delivery triggers an AWS Lambda function. The Lambda function processes the logs, extracts relevant fields, maps IP addresses to country IDs, and then inserts this processed data into Amazon Elasticsearch Service. Elasticsearch, configured with anomaly detectors, monitors these access patterns for each client. If an anomaly is detected, it triggers an alert via Amazon SNS, which sends email notifications to the Mobilewala service team (represented as a UserCompanyDeveloper). The nodes are identified directly from the visual icons and labels on the whiteboard, while the connections are based on the drawn arrows and confirmed by the transcript's description of the data flow.

graph.name: Mobilewala S3 Access Log Anomaly Detection
graph.notes: This architecture by Mobilewala uses S3 access logs, Lambda, Elasticsearch's anomaly detection feature, and SNS to proactively detect suspicious access patterns to client data stored in S3 buckets. Lambda processes logs to add custom fields like client name and geographic details for effective anomaly detection.

nodes.name: Log Processor Lambda
nodes.notes: Triggered when new logs land in the S3 Access Logs bucket. It parses log values, extracts fields like client name, maps IP addresses to country IDs, and adds custom fields before inserting data into Elasticsearch.

nodes.name: Anomaly Detector
nodes.notes: Amazon Elasticsearch Service (now OpenSearch Service) is used with its anomaly detection feature. It learns access patterns for each client (filtered by client name) and uses the numeric country ID to detect anomalies. Originally referred to as Amazon Elasticsearch Service in the transcript.

nodes.name: Anomaly Alert Topic
nodes.notes: Amazon SNS is used to send email notifications to the service team when Elasticsearch detects an anomaly.
